designSystem.visualDirection: modern, premium, restrained colour, natural realistic photography when pedagogically useful

screens.title: Pronunciation · Listen & Order
screens.layout: four large word clusters in a 2×2 grid with one compact number field per word
screens.teacherAction: Check Responses, replay, then Show answer in each number field
screens.visualAid: large waveform and current sound focus; no tiny table

screens.title: Listen Again & Repeat
screens.layout: single sound-focus card with segmented waveform, large Replay control and speaking cue
screens.teacherAction: control pacing and replay; no fabricated transcript
screens.sourcePolicy: Use the source recording only; do not invent printed sentences

screens.title: Sound Sort
screens.layout: three large sound zones /æ/ · /ɑː/ · /ʌ/ with draggable word chips
screens.studentAction: listen, repeat, then drag each word to the sound zone
screens.teacherAction: Responses/Check first, then reveal correct grouping
screens.visualPolicy: strong typographic phonics design; no decorative photos

screens.title: Find the Differences
screens.layout: 15-second original-scene memory view → changed scene → numbered hotspots
screens.model: The photographer isn't taking a photo of the model now; he's taking a photo of the thief.
screens.studentAction: identify one changed person at a time and type or say the contrast
screens.teacherAction: Timer, Responses, then character-by-character Show answer
answers: The model isn't standing by the fountain; she's talking to the journalist.
The artist isn't painting a picture; she's showing a child the picture.
The journalist isn't writing in his notebook; he's talking to the model.
The bank guard isn't standing near the door of the bank; he's having a cup of coffee.
The photographer isn't taking a photo of the model; he's taking a photo of the thief.
The police officer isn't sitting in his car; he is running after the woman with the bag.
screens.visualRule: use two distinct realistic scenes, not the repeated seven-job photo wall

screens.title: What's My Job? · Live Mystery
screens.layout: secret job card for Teacher/selected learner + large clue cards + whole-class QR response strip

jobRoutine: Do you talk to other people?

screens.studentAction: ask yes/no questions and submit one final job guess through QR/Responses
screens.teacherAction: run one mystery round at a time; reveal only after guesses are collected
screens.cognitiveLevel: infer from evidence + distinguish NOW vs ROUTINE

screens.title: Tom · Match Questions & Answers
screens.layout: large photo zone + seven question chips + seven draggable answer cards; split 4+3 if required for readability
questions: What kind of person is he?
How do you feel about doing this kind of thing?
answers: He's tall and he's got short fair hair.
He's wearing white shorts and a red T-shirt.
I wouldn't like to do this.
Because I don't like the smell of paint.
screens.teacherAction: Check first; Show answer reveals matched cards and then the seven-part speaking framework
screens.visualRule: one strong natural photo, not multiple oversized photos

screens.title: Describe the Young Woman
screens.layout: one full-height workplace photo at controlled size + seven large prompt chips + one response panel
questions: What kind of person is she?
How do you feel about doing this kind of thing?
model: She's slim and she's got long, wavy hair.
She's reading an email and eating a sandwich.
I wouldn't like to do this.
Because I don't like office work. It's boring.
screens.studentAction: plan from chips, speak, then submit a brief self-check or text summary
screens.teacherAction: listen/read Responses and reveal the model only after production
screens.visualRule: photo must be natural, contemporary and different from previous job images

screens.title: Memory Recall Challenge
screens.layout: seven numbered empty slots arranged as a speaking-framework arc; one prompt appears at a time
targetQuestions: What kind of person is he/she?
How do you feel about doing this kind of thing?
screens.studentAction: reconstruct the seven questions from memory
screens.teacherAction: collect Responses, then Show answer one slot at a time
screens.visualPolicy: text-led memory task; no unnecessary photograph

screens.title: Photograph A / Photograph B
screens.layout: two balanced photo cards with Part A / Part B tabs and a persistent seven-item peer checklist
screens.studentAction: Student A speaks for 60–90 seconds; Student B ticks heard content, then swap
screens.teacherAction: Timer + Responses for peer checklist; model language optional, not compulsory
screens.visualRule: two genuinely different natural photos; no repeated crop or mirrored duplicate

screens.title: Tom · Reading Part 5
screens.layout: one sentence at a time with four large option cards; after Check, rejected distractors fade sequentially

items.prompt: Tom ____ a tin of yellow paint.

screens.studentAction: choose the best answer and optionally mark one rejected distractor
screens.teacherAction: Check Responses, discuss elimination, then Show answer
screens.strategy: If you are not sure which word is correct, decide which words are wrong, and why.

screens.title: Irena · Reading Part 5
screens.layout: reuse the same clean exam component, but with new content and no decorative photo

items.prompt: Irena usually ____ a sandwich for lunch.

screens.teacherAction: Check first, then Show answer and reasoning cue in place

screens.title: Unit 3 Exit Challenge · Job City
screens.layout: one coherent realistic Job City visual with airport, office, shop, garage, studio and bank zones; reveal one challenge at a time
screens.studentAction: complete mixed hotspot, tense, short-answer and speaking challenges
screens.teacherAction: Responses summary + selective Show answer after each challenge
screens.visualRule: single integrated scene replaces repeated disconnected stock pictures
